lens: Duolingo-style gamification: skill tree of sales skills, streaks, XP, leagues, bite-size levels
name: Game Tape Skill Path
one_liner: A skill tree, XP and streaks wrap every rep in a dark game-tape coaching stage, so practice feels like a season and every live call is scored.
lens_followed_or_changed: Followed: skill tree of sales skills, XP, day streaks, bite-size levels, leagues. Changed: Duolingo's mascot, gems and candy palette would read as childish to call-center managers and training buyers, so the same mechanics use a sports-broadcast game-tape language (dark stage for calls, mono numerals, sparing gold). Leagues are opt-in and team-scoped. Self-scores: A 8, B 7, C 8. Business: F1 6 (streak retention helps, but Second Nature and Hyperbound are funded), F2 7 (manager heatmap and team leagues sell to training firms and call centers), F3 3 (clearly worth building as open core, and the grant funds the core).

ui_stack.name: shadcn/ui on Radix Primitives
ui_stack.role: Component layer for every screen: dialogs, sheets, tabs, combobox, toasts, forms
ui_stack.why: MIT licensed and copied into the repo, so contributors own the code; Tailwind-native and accessible by default, with no vendor lock-in for an open-source project.

ui_stack.name: Tailwind CSS v4 with CSS-variable tokens
ui_stack.role: Styling and theming; replaces the hand-rolled .card and .btn classes
ui_stack.why: Semantic tokens let the dark stage and the light app share one system; shadcn documents this setup.

ui_stack.name: Motion (motion/react)
ui_stack.role: XP pops, score count-up, skill-node unlock, orb and cue entrance
ui_stack.why: Spring physics with a reduced-motion fallback, light enough for the live call route.

ui_stack.name: Recharts via shadcn chart
ui_stack.role: Score curves, progress radials, manager heatmap
ui_stack.why: Themed through the same tokens, so every chart matches the rest of the app.

ui_stack.name: Hand-built SVG skill tree (@xyflow/react only past 60 nodes)
ui_stack.role: Skill tree on Progress and the pre-call briefing
ui_stack.why: Around 30 nodes fit in a small SVG; React Flow stays as an escape hatch if the tree grows.

ui_stack.name: Lucide React plus custom SVG badges
ui_stack.role: Icons, plus skill and league badge artwork
ui_stack.why: Keeps the existing icon set; badges give the game layer its own look without cartoon mascots.

ui_stack.name: next/font: Bricolage Grotesque, Inter, JetBrains Mono
ui_stack.role: Display titles; UI and transcript text; timers and scores
ui_stack.why: Moves away from the default Inter plus Sora template feel; tabular mono numerals stop timers and XP from jittering.

palette.use: Live call, debrief header and landing hero: the game-tape dark stage
XP, level rings, unlocks and league badges only
Streak chips and day dots only
Mastered skill nodes and criteria at or above target
Objection alerts and End and grade
Model lab badges naming an OpenAI model; never the OpenAI logo

design_language.typography: Bricolage Grotesque 600-700 for page titles and the grade letter; Inter 400-600 for UI, transcript and body at 16px; JetBrains Mono with tabular numerals for timers, XP and scores. Type scale 1.25; transcript line height 1.5.
design_language.shape_and_depth: 16px card radius, 12px controls, 1px #E2E8F0 borders on light surfaces and 1px white at 10% on the stage. Shadows only on floating cues and sheets. Primary buttons get a 2px darker bottom edge that compresses on press, a light nod to tactile game buttons without gloss.
design_language.motion: Springs of 180 to 260ms. XP pops rise 24px and fade. Skill nodes fill with a 400ms ring sweep. Scores count up on debrief entry. Cues slide in from the rail edge. Reduced-motion users get the end state instantly.
design_language.iconography: Lucide at 1.75px stroke. Flame only for streaks, bolt only for XP, hexagonal custom badges for skills and leagues. No emoji in product UI.
design_language.theme_modes: Light is the default app theme. The dark stage applies to the live call, debrief header and landing hero in both themes. Honour prefers-color-scheme plus a manual toggle; both modes use the same semantic tokens.

navigation_and_ia: Desktop: a 72px icon rail with Path (home), Library, Live, Debriefs, Progress and, for org admins, Team. The top bar carries a streak flame chip, an XP chip with a level ring, and the avatar. Mobile: bottom tabs Path, Library, Call (raised centre button), Progress, Me. Start call is one tap from every screen. The scenario dropdown is retired; Library owns scenario choice, with Build with AI as the first tile. Settings, MFA and the Model lab live under Me.

live_coaching_and_scoring: Coaching runs on a second, cheap text model (GPT-4.1 mini by default) reading transcript turns in parallel, so the persona never coaches and its voice stays natural. Cues are capped at one per 20 to 25 seconds, with Off, Subtle and Active modes. Rubric meters update after each rep turn, with evidence chips on the transcript, not after the call. Objection alerts name the rubric criterion they threaten. The debrief states which grader ran: model or keyword heuristic. Heuristic scores show an Estimate badge and withhold XP, fixing the fallback warning seen on today's debrief. Self-score D 5.2: meets the baseline only if cue latency stays under 2 seconds and throttling ships; reaches about 5.8 with moment replay on the debrief timeline.
persona_library_and_wizard: Personas ship as versioned files in the repo, with at least ten per sales job at launch across SDR cold call, AE discovery, SaaS, insurance, mortgage, real estate, solar, home services, auto, medical devices, B2B procurement, recruiting, retail, customer success and collections. Each persona carries objection tags, difficulty, rubric weights and a talk track, so the library works as a curriculum. Filters: role, industry, difficulty, objection type. The wizard takes a job description, product URL, CRM notes, ICP or pasted call; a GPT model returns structured persona, scenario and rubric drafts with provenance per field. A two-minute dry run must pass before save. Self-score E 5.6: the faceted library and wizard meet the standard; the dry-run gate and human-reviewed personas push it higher.
signature_moments: Hot-streak flame lights after three rubric hits in a row, with a one-line XP pop.
A violet now-cue card arrives mid-call; tapping it pins it for the next rep turn.
Debrief: the skill node rises from level 2 to 3 with a ring sweep as the grade lands.
Objection cards collect per branch; beating the price objection three times unlocks a Price Pro badge.
Model lab chip under each cue shows which OpenAI model ran, with latency and token cost.
Author a persona, merge the PR, and your handle gets a Persona author badge on the library card.
openai_fund_angle: Each OpenAI model has a visible job. The Realtime API runs the voice persona. A small GPT model (GPT-4.1 mini by default) reads each turn to drive cues and grading. A larger GPT model drafts personas in the wizard. A Model lab panel, under Me and on each debrief, lists which model ran each step with latency and token cost per call, showing reviewers efficient use of API credits. Landing and README carry a text strip reading Built on OpenAI Realtime API and GPT models; no logo without brand approval. Contributors: the Library is the contribution surface. Add a persona exports a file and opens a prefilled PR, the skill tree marks open contribution nodes, and contributor XP shows on profiles. The repo's PR review, release notes and maintainer triage will run on Codex, matching the Codex for Open Source criteria.

inspirations.source: Second Nature vs Hyperbound comparison (secondnature.ai, vendor-written)
inspirations.borrowed: Competitor framing: AI buyer-persona library and video roleplay. Vendor claims are unverified and not to be repeated.
Copy-in accessible components and CSS-variable theming on Tailwind.

implementation.migration_path: Phase 1 (about 1 week): Tailwind v4 and shadcn tokens, replace the .card and .btn classes, add the stage token. Phase 2 (1-2 weeks): live-call coaching rail and debrief, since they carry the grant demo. Phase 3: persona library and wizard, seeded with 10 personas per job. Phase 4: skill tree, streaks, opt-in leagues and the manager view. Keep /trainer and /dashboard routes; add parity tests for voice and text modes and visual checks at 390px in both themes.

risks: Gamification can read as childish to enterprise buyers; mitigate with the restrained stage palette and opt-in leagues.
Cue latency and noise: the 2-second budget and throttle are unproven; test on recorded calls before the grant demo.
Today's debrief already falls back to a keyword heuristic; XP built on heuristic scores would reward noise, so XP must be withheld then.
Tailwind 3 to 4 plus shadcn touches every screen; regression risk without visual tests in both themes and at 390px.
Competitor marketing claims (Second Nature cites 34% faster ramp) are unverified; do not repeat them in the README.
Persona quality: 150 personas need human review; ship a rubric-quality gate and label unreviewed personas as drafts.
